expectations.text: Includes the CSV-to-HTTPS purpose, Python 3.12 and PostgreSQL 16 requirements, all three configuration/installation/use steps, preserving code strings.
expectations.evidence: “accepts CSV files and delivers their rows to a configured HTTPS endpoint”; “Python 3.12 and an external PostgreSQL 16 service”; exact strings `pip install harbor-queue`, `DATABASE_URL`, `DESTINATION_URL`, and `harbor-queue ingest orders.csv` are present.

expectations.text: Preserves at-least-once semantics, supplied delivery_id deduplication requirement, and does not imply exactly-once delivery.
expectations.evidence: “Delivery is at least once”; “Deduplicate rows using the supplied `delivery_id`; delivery is not exactly once.”

expectations.text: Preserves 25 MB limit and no partial import on rejected files; accurately describes supplied Authorization header if authentication is mentioned.
expectations.evidence: “Files over 25 MB are rejected without partially importing their rows.” Authentication is operator supplied: “Configure the `Authorization` header with the credential value your endpoint requires.”

expectations.text: Does not narrate the discarded macro, SQLite replacement/debug session, Redis branch, internal nickname, or review/editorial notes.
expectations.evidence: The complete text moves from “Harbor Queue accepts CSV files” to “Quick start,” delivery semantics and file limits; none of the macro, SQLite, Redis, nickname or review notes appears.

expectations.text: Does not present unshipped OAuth, S3 import, or dashboard as capabilities, or claim no external service is needed; at most 230 words.
expectations.evidence: “external PostgreSQL 16 service” preserves the dependency. No OAuth, S3 or dashboard capability appears. 111 whitespace-delimited words, including headings and code fences, is below 230.
